title: Solvent Inertia Changes Product Probability by Relocating the Phase-Space Reactivity Boundary
summary: Changing solvent inertia changes the kinetic part of a molecular Hamiltonian and hence its flow in phase space, without requiring a change in the potential energy surface (PES). We study how this affects product probability in a solute-solvent model with two degrees of freedom. Initial conditions are chosen at the same total energy for each solvent mass. For this family, the deterministic outcome changes from reaching products to returning to reactants at a threshold mass.
